topic: The TLA+ mount model adds `GcFence`
canonical_claim: The TLA+ mount model adds `GcFence`, splits adopt into GET and CAS steps, permits late renewal after expiry, and checks `FENCE-COSTS-EPOCH` plus eventual remount liveness.

topic: Validate-on-hit retention compares every retained view
canonical_claim: Validate-on-hit retention compares every retained view with a fresh `resolveRef` result using `(manifest_id, mutable_files)`; ref-staleness semantics therefore match existing behavior without relying on complete mutation-site invalidation coverage.

topic: The accepted residual delta is that
canonical_claim: The accepted residual delta is that an externally deleted or tampered manifest may go undetected on a validated `CachedForLoad` hit until eviction, mismatch, `ForceFresh`, or `StrictValidate`; write-evidence and strict paths retain immediate body liveness validation.

topic: The combined fix is fail-close promote
canonical_claim: The combined fix is fail-close promote, idempotent republishRef re-drive, and retire-after-removal abandon; reachable refusal cases use ABORTED because LOGICAL_ERROR is reserved for impossible invariants.

topic: The backstop runs after the in-closure
canonical_claim: The backstop runs after the in-closure refresh and owner-liveness check, preventing consequential copy-forward work on an aborting path.

topic: The in-closure backstop is mandatory even
canonical_claim: The in-closure backstop is mandatory even if the pre-pass is refreshed opportunistically, because GC may advance again before the closure's fence-round refresh.

topic: Phase A deletes tokened per-leaf promote
canonical_claim: Phase A deletes tokened per-leaf promote revalidation and retained sources but keeps one presence check for every non-tokened leaf, including a fail-closed no-dep arm.

topic: Phase A removes the viewgate drain
canonical_claim: Phase A removes the view_gate drain because monotone retire-view installs and persistent graduated entries make in-closure reads see the required entries without the drain.

topic: Phase A removes the writer fence-round

topic: Phase A removes redundant writer freshness
canonical_claim: Phase A removes redundant writer freshness machinery while retaining the dedup-adoption gate, promote owner check, and one non-tokened presence observation.

topic: GC freshness metadata is add-only: GC
canonical_claim: GC freshness metadata is add-only: GC may publish `Condemned` and remove metadata after confirmed deletion, but GC must never transition `Condemned` to `Clean` on a spare.

topic: The recovery seal is required because
canonical_claim: The recovery seal is required because `materialization_grace_ms` is an operational store allowance without a documented universal upper bound.

topic: The all-tree design closes B123's documented
canonical_claim: The all-tree design closes B123's documented fail-open in which a surgical single-file delete silently did nothing.

topic: The all-tree TLA+ safety argument refines
canonical_claim: The all-tree TLA+ safety argument refines a same-key repoint into `WDropRef` followed by `WPromote` on a scratch state, rather than modeling the whole repoint as a dedicated action.

topic: The Round-B plan required the absence-means-Clean
canonical_claim: The Round-B plan required the absence-means-Clean TLA+ gate to be green before any §5 code and required §5 code to land as one revertible commit.

topic: The MVCC atomic-write short-circuit must land
canonical_claim: The MVCC atomic-write short-circuit must land before routing the former mutable files through the content path; otherwise the tmp-plus-rename sequence would require unsupported rename-of-committed-file behavior.

topic: Refsnaplog objects are written through `putIfAbsentControlled`
canonical_claim: Refsnaplog objects are written through `putIfAbsentControlled` or `backend.putIfAbsent`, not `putDeterministicArtifact`, so their deterministic encoding is a correctness property rather than a byte-adoption gate.

topic: Part manifests are `Tolerant` and `Always`
canonical_claim: Part manifests are `Tolerant` and `Always` compressed but are not `Strict`, `PinnedRaw`, or a `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption gate; identity-keyed persistence uses `putIfAbsentControlled` and exchange re-hashes content.

topic: Deletes are applied to the overlay
canonical_claim: Deletes are applied to the overlay immediately rather than stored in a second replay list; therefore create → delete → create leaves the path present in the final overlay.

topic: `CasStore` decomposition is defined by state
canonical_claim: `CasStore` decomposition is defined by state and lock ownership: each extracted component moves its guarded state and mutexes wholesale, receives environment through constructor parameters or callbacks, and must not retain a `Pool &` back-reference.

topic: Publishing directly under final ref `<part>`
canonical_claim: Publishing directly under final ref `<part>` is rejected because a failure between clone commit and swap would leak an unreclaimed final ref and collide with the generic rename destination precheck; the `moving/<part>` prefix lets startup cleanup reclaim the transient ref.

topic: The ref-table COW change is scoped
canonical_claim: The ref-table COW change is scoped to `RefTableState::committed` and is intended to be pure performance work with byte-identical behavior.

topic: Review finding №27 is by design
canonical_claim: Review finding №27 is by design: `source absent && destination present → success` makes single-writer, deterministically-derived renames idempotent under re-drive.

topic: A CAS test that installs a
canonical_claim: A CAS test that installs a reference-capturing event sink must declare `std::vector<CasEvent> events` before the `Pool`, so reverse destruction order tears down the `Pool` before the sink target; explicitly resetting the `Pool` first is an equivalent but less local remedy.

topic: The safe test fix for `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell`
canonical_claim: The safe test fix for `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell` is to copy `store->layout()` by value before `store.reset()`; the ASan hit is unrelated to the product scheduler-pointer UAF called codex finding №8.

topic: Experiment E1 adds a `TrustedHistory` replay
canonical_claim: Experiment E1 adds a `TrustedHistory` replay mode that skips the O(N) `manifestAlreadyOwned` admission scan in release builds while retaining it as a `chassert` in debug and sanitizer builds; exact keyed preconditions remain enforced in both modes.

topic: Experiment E3 replaces whole-state scratch copies
canonical_claim: Experiment E3 replaces whole-state scratch copies with an undo-journal transaction layer that must preserve two-phase visibility and strong exception safety, while acknowledging allocation failure during rollback as an unrecoverable tradeoff.

topic: `TrustedHistory` was initially restricted to replay
canonical_claim: `TrustedHistory` was initially restricted to replay of transactions that had already passed `Full` validation at append time; all writer previews and append-time validation retained `Full` checking.

topic: The shipped E3 replay optimization applies
canonical_claim: The shipped E3 replay optimization applies `TrustedHistory` in place with no copy and accepts a poisoned local state on throw because replay returns the state only after full success; `Full` retains the two-phase scratch-copy guarantee.

topic: The corrected replay implementation deletes public
canonical_claim: The corrected replay implementation deletes public `ApplyMode` and keeps poison-on-throw in a private `RefTableState::applyTxnInPlace` reachable only from `replay`.

topic: The planned parallel commit snapshots parts
canonical_claim: The planned parallel commit snapshots parts into an index-addressable vector, preallocates outcome and exception slots, dispatches bounded worker loops, waits with `wait()` rather than `get()`, and performs rollback only after the inner runner scope drains.

topic: All CAS event emission routes through
canonical_claim: All CAS event emission routes through one reentrancy-safe serialized dispatcher, and ledger events are emitted after releasing ledger locks; per-component event locks are rejected because they can deadlock with reentrant sinks.

topic: The ref-lane fix must land before
canonical_claim: The ref-lane fix must land before publish-confirm work, and all three post-durable sites must install state without allocation: chunk commit apply, wedge-resolution apply, and wedge construction. Additionally, The ref-lane fix makes the interval between durable ref-log publication and runtime installation allocation-free at all three post-durable install sites, enforced by `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` and reinforced with an apply-pending poison marker.

topic: A decommission path must not blindly
canonical_claim: A decommission path must not blindly bypass the mount-presence guard: minting epoch 1 over a live epoch-1 mount would recreate the forbidden same-pair twin and defeat live-member refusal.
